subject: Pricing: step-down rebate, cap exceptions, and per-token smoothing options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Porter <emily.porter@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing options for Hosted API commit (attachments)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the convo yesterday. As promised, attached are three scenario worksheets that show both a standard marginal-band approach and two smoothing alternatives we discussed. Quick summary:

- Scenario A (marginal bands): clean breakpoint pricing at 100M / 300M / 1B tokens; best unit cost at top band but larger cliffs.
- Scenario B (blended smoothing): monthly blended rate with a three-month reconciliation to avoid cliff jumps.
- Scenario C (step-down rebate): commit-based step-downs that trigger rebates applied retrospectively each quarter; preserves predictable unit economics for Horizon.

Key asks from our side to move forward:
1) Target 12–18 month total commit range (ballpark tokens/month).
2) Preferred reconciliation cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
3) Any hard caps/ceilings you need for budget planning (e.g., max monthly spend).

I attached Redwood-Pricing-Scenario-3.xlsx and Horizon-Commit-Rollout-Table.csv. If you can share the commit profile you expect in Q1–Q3, Jordan and I will produce a blended worked example that highlights month-to-month invoices and a worst-case cap.

Thanks — we should be able to produce a single-sheet proposal you can take to procurement by Thursday.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: Pricing options for Hosted API commit (attachments)

Marcus —

Thanks for the deck and the scenarios — looked through them with our finance and procurement leads. A few things on our side:

- Procurement will push back on pure marginal cliffs (Scenario A). They prefer a blended or capped approach to avoid surprise spikes if usage shifts.
- Our finance team wants an explicit monthly cap option (hard cap or overage smoothing) since month-to-month budgets are reviewed by the CFO.
- Can you provide an example with a $250k/month cap and annual true-up? Also: we need a proposal that shows both a blended per-token rate and an equivalent marginal-band schedule so we can compare.

One more ask: Horizon needs limited contract language exceptions on the SLA credits and a carve-out for certain PHI-handling workloads (they'll route PHI to a private deployment later this year). Procurement wants to see what exceptions Redwood would accept before we circulate a redline.

Emily Porter

Jordan — can you run the blended-vs-marginal worked example and include an optional smoothing factor that effectively amortizes band cliffs over a 3-month window? If we show numbers (invoice vs true-up) for a 12-month term with quarterly rebates, I think procurement will be comfortable.

Priyom — pricing/finance: what are our minimums on offering a hard monthly customer cap? Can we cross-cancel with committed tokens or do we need a credit mechanism? Also, if we allow a step-down rebate (Scenario C) we need language about how overage vs commit shortfall reconciliation works.

Laura — legal will likely handle the carve-outs. Can you flag the typical SLA carve we grant for private-PHI routing and what exceptions are off-limits?

Marcus

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing options for Hosted API commit — ask from Horizon (cap request + exceptions)

Marcus / team —

Attached is a short worked example (tab "Blended_vs_Marginal"). Summary in plain language:

- Hybrid proposal: keep marginal bands (100M / 300M / 1B) for list pricing, but offer Horizon a monthly blended invoice rate with a 3-month smoothing window. Practically: each month we compute the marginal invoice; then we average the last 3 months to produce the billed blended unit price. This avoids one-off cliffs while preserving our marginal economics for high-usage months.

- Cap option: we can set a contractual monthly spend cap ($250k) and convert any eligible overage into a ledger credit that reduces the next monthly blended invoice (so customer never exceeds the cap on invoice). Ledger credits are funded by Redwood and reconciled against the quarterly true-up. In effect: customer sees predictability, we preserve long-term unit economics via quarterly true-up.

- Step-down rebate detail (Scenario C): if annual committed tokens are met, we issue rebates at each step-down threshold retrospectively on a quarterly cadence. If shortfalls occur, rebates are clawed back pro rata.

Numbers (example):
- List marginal rates: Band1 (0–100M): $0.0009/1k tokens; Band2 (100M–300M): $0.0007/1k; Band3 (300M+): $0.0005/1k.
- Blended invoice example (month with 180M tokens): marginal invoice = $X; 3-month blended billed rate = marginal invoices averaged -> yields $0.00082/1k billed.

Risks / asks:
1) Finance needs to confirm ledger-credit accounting treatment for the cap (Priyom).
2) Legal to confirm SLA carve language (Laura).

I'll attach the workbook export and the summary slide.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Revised proposal: blended invoice + $250k monthly cap (proposal + MAP)

Emily / team —

Appended is our revised commercial proposal and a short mutual action plan (MAP). High level:

- Commercial: we propose the hybrid approach Jordan outlined — marginal list bands (for transparency) with an optional 3-month blended invoice that smooths cliffs. We will implement a $250k contractual monthly cap option. Ledger credits will be applied to the next blended invoice and reconciled quarterly.
- Rebate: Step-down rebates remain available if annual committed tokens are achieved; rebates are issued quarterly and clawed back pro rata for shortfalls.
- Legal exceptions: Laura has proposed a narrow SLA carve for PHI-handled workloads that are routed to Horizon's private deployment; otherwise standard SLA applies. We are not able to accept unlimited carve-outs on uptime guarantees.

Attachments: Redwood-Pricing-Scenario-3.xlsx (updated), Redwood-Terms-Exceptions.docx, MAP-Horizon-Redwood-2026Q4.pdf

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review term sheet and indicate which commercial option you prefer (blended invoice + cap or marginal-only).
2) If blended + cap chosen, sign the LOI/term sheet; we will provision the ledger-credit mechanism and set up quarterly true-up reporting.
3) Legal: Laura will send a tracked redline for the exceptions doc by Wednesday for your procurement team.

If you want, we can hop on a 30-minute call Wednesday morning to walk procurement through the blended math and the MAP. DocuSign link below for the term sheet if you want to start circulation.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABCD-REDWOOD-HZ-1087

Thanks again — we think this approach gives Horizon budget predictability while aligning long-term unit economics.
